title: Cross-harness contract matrix
summary: Run equivalent scenarios through API, MCP, and Pi and compare normalized outcomes.
description: Define a shared scenario matrix whose cases can be executed through the HTTP API, MCP tools, and Pi adapter commands/tools. Normalize identifiers, status payloads, error categories, and persisted plan snapshots so equivalent operations can be compared without coupling tests to transport formatting. Include create/update/delete flows, invalid validation inputs, references, requirements links, status rollups, handoff proposal/confirmation, archive behavior, repair, load/stop lifecycle, and resume context. Record intentional transport differences explicitly and fail on semantic divergence. This phase is the compatibility gate ensuring that every harness exposes the same planner behavior while preserving each harness's native protocol.

tasks.title: Define normalized adapter outcomes and persisted snapshots
tasks.description:
Implement shared normalization for API JSON, MCP structured content, Pi tool/notification responses, and persisted `.planner` snapshots. Normalize UUID-bearing payloads to composite F/P/T references where appropriate, classify validation/permission/not-found/terminal-state errors, and compare canonical entity/status/handoff data while preserving intentional transport differences. Document the fields that must match across harnesses.

---
**Completion summary:**
Implemented the shared cross-harness normalization layer for P059 in `test/helpers/runner.mjs`: Pi `details` now merge with MCP `structuredContent`, normalized outcomes expose `errorCategory`, canonical `status`, extracted composite references, and optional normalized persisted snapshots. Extended `test/helpers/fixtures.mjs` `readPlanSnapshot()` to capture `.local/resume.json`, `.local/activity.json`, and archived handoff markdown payloads so snapshot assertions can compare persisted planner state. Updated `test/scenario-matrix.mjs` to document the richer normalized contract (`errorCategory`, `status`, `reference`, `textIncludes`, `snapshot`) and pinned representative scenarios to those fields. Added `test/result-normalization.test.mjs` covering tool/API normalization, not-found + validation classification, persisted snapshot ref normalization, and assertion support for the richer contract. Validation: `node --test test/result-normalization.test.mjs test/matrix-consistency.test.mjs` passed (17 tests).

tasks.title: Run validation and error-parity scenarios across API MCP and Pi
tasks.description:
Execute the same invalid feature, phase, task, requirement, reference, checklist, reorder, and handoff inputs through HTTP API, MCP, and Pi. Compare normalized error categories, blocked-write behavior, field paths/messages where contractually stable, and final filesystem snapshots. Record explicit differences only where a harness protocol requires different wrapping, ensuring no adapter silently accepts input rejected by core.

---
**Completion summary:**
Implemented the validation/error-parity wave for P059 across API, MCP, and Pi. Added `test/error-parity.test.mjs`, registering targeted API/MCP/Pi executors against the shared scenario matrix for negative create/ref/requirement/handoff/lifecycle cases and asserting parity on normalized error categories plus persisted snapshots. Extended `test/scenario-matrix.mjs` negative scenarios with explicit `errorCategory` expectations and refined `test/helpers/runner.mjs` normalization to infer semantic tool failures from plain-text adapter responses, carry richer validation classifications, and prefer HTTP `message` payloads when present. Fixed real adapter behavior in `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts` by validating requirement titles and linked phase refs, guarding empty phase/task titles before persistence, and rejecting generic explicit handoff titles; mirrored the generic-title rejection fix in `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts`. Rebuilt `@agent-plan/pi-adapter` and `@agent-plan/mcp`. Validation: `node --test test/error-parity.test.mjs test/result-normalization.test.mjs test/matrix-consistency.test.mjs` passed (32 tests).

tasks.title: Run lifecycle, requirements, handoff, and resume parity scenarios
tasks.description:

Compare canonical persisted state, active/archive lists, handoff reasons/history, composite references, and lifecycle side effects across all entry points.

---
**Completion summary:**
Fixed cross-harness handoff/resume lifecycle regression. `planner-load` now explicitly treats pending handoffs as read-only context and forbids implicit show/clear; the generated CLI command router mirrors the same rule. `buildRecap` now ends with the `🌐 Web UI:` line so Codex can render the dashboard address consistently. Core lifecycle cleanup now archives a handoff only when every task is `done` or `canceled`, covering the prior all-canceled/rejected gap; writes archive a superseded prior handoff and retain only the newest active version; explicit clear remains manual. Updated Pi wording and the surface inventory to match. Added/updated core tests for replacement and all-canceled archival and an MCP regression test proving `planner-load` retains a pending handoff and its final nonempty output line is Web UI.

Validated: `pnpm test` (360/360), `pnpm build`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm plugins:check`, targeted core/MCP suites, `pnpm test:matrix`, and `git diff --check`. Changes are ready locally; release commit/push/bump pending the requested publish step.

tasks.title: Fix phase-read contract and explicit multi-active task starts
tasks.description:
Repair two cross-harness regressions observed while operating the planner in heca. First, `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` registers `planner-phase-show` (around lines 630–644) and calls `text(..., { linkedRequirements })`: Claude Code renders this sparse structured payload and hides the otherwise correct text content containing the phase title and long description. Define a complete structured phase read model (identity/ref, title, summary, description when `full=true`, derived status, task count, and `linkedRequirements`) and validate it through the real MCP harness as Claude Code consumes it. Second, `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` task-start logic (around lines 1019–1084) and the matching `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts` logic (around lines 3924–3980) treat `recommendNextTask()` as a hard authorization gate. When multiple tasks are already `in-progress`, its intentionally advisory `conflict` result prevents an explicitly requested task (such as T416) from starting. Preserve automatic-selection safety and conflict warnings, but allow an explicit task-start request for a valid ready task without requiring unrelated active tasks to be falsely completed/blocked. Confirm behavior is consistent in MCP and Pi, preserve dependency and terminal-state protection, and add regression tests using the real MCP server and Pi host fixture.

---
**Completion summary:**
Fixed the cross-harness regressions locally (not committed). `planner-phase-show` in `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` now returns a complete structured `phase` model (human ref, title, summary, derived status, task count, and description on `full=true`) alongside linked requirements, so Claude Code no longer hides the phase description by rendering only `{linkedRequirements}`. Added a real MCP regression test that reads the structured response as a Claude-style client.

Added the harness-agnostic `checkExplicitTaskStart` in `packages/plan-core/src/task-selection.ts`. MCP and Pi task-start handlers now use it to enforce real availability/dependency rules while treating priority, a single active task, and multiple active tasks as advisories rather than hard denials for an explicit task reference. Responses distinguish priority, active-task, and active-work-conflict advisories. This allows an explicitly chosen task such as T416 to start without falsely closing unrelated tasks. Also fixed approved deviation activation so it remains reliable even when recommendation output points at already active work; preserved the existing approved waiting-task exception.

Added unit + real MCP/Pi adapter regression coverage. Validation passed: targeted suite 59/59, `pnpm check`, and `pnpm test` 359/359 (baseline coverage line 82.92%, branch 73.4%, functions 78.7%). Modified files remain uncommitted on `next`: core selector/tests, MCP handler/tests, Pi handler/tests.
tasks.notes: While executing the cross-harness regression suite, an existing deviation test exposed a coupled third defect: `recommendNextTask()` returns the current active task before inspecting an approved deviation, so starting the deviation’s temporary task after another explicit start does not transition the deviation to `active`. The task-start fix will activate an approved matching deviation directly from persisted `workDeviations`, rather than relying on advisory recommendation output. This preserves the deviation/resume lifecycle under explicit multi-active starts.

tasks.title: Fix resume-required header layout and keep full checkpoint details in task view
tasks.description: The current resume-required presentation in `packages/plan-web-ui/src/components/layout/app-shell.tsx` renders `ResumeSnapshot` directly inside the sticky focus header when `task.pauseSnapshot` exists. In real data this pushes long checkpoint prose into the header, creates an oversized card, and can introduce an internal scrollbar, as seen in the user screenshot. The full checkpoint narrative already belongs on the task detail surface (`packages/plan-web-ui/src/routes/task-detail/route.tsx` with data from `packages/plan-web-ui/src/routes/task-detail/loader.ts`) and should remain there. Implement a compact header-only presentation that preserves canonical task status plus the secondary resume marker from T289, shows at most a short summary/action hint in the sticky header, and leaves the full Why paused / Work checkpoint / Resume from / How to resume content inside the task view. Update the related Web UI tests in `packages/plan-web-ui/test/entity-references-and-updates.test.tsx` (and any route-level tests if needed) so the header no longer renders the verbose snapshot block while task detail still renders the full checkpoint content. Preserve the current pending-resume semantics and do not regress the distinction between canonical workflow status and resume-required markers.
